about: The living-workforce intent taxonomy (docs/LIVING-WORKFORCE.md §3). Each intent says what triggers it, when it may play, on which channels, with which slots, under which Ambience, and how it is pre-voiced. The engine (packages/expressions) reads this file; archetype and signature packs supply the lines. Times are milliseconds; 'EOT' is the end of the owner's turn (TurnAssembler close, push-to-talk release or Send).

owner.speech.pause.description: Local VAD: the owner paused inside an utterance addressed to this agent (push-to-talk held, or hands-free).

owner.turn.end.description: End of the owner's turn: Send, push-to-talk release, or TurnAssembler close. Carries the affect cues sniffed from the text or final transcript.

owner.turn.resumed.description: The owner kept talking after a closed turn (TurnAssembler reopened); every pending reflex for that turn is cancelled.

owner.barge_in.description: Owner speech confirmed over agent audio (EXPERIENCE §5.3) or the owner took the floor in a room.

owner.message.while_speaking.description: The owner sent a new message while this agent's voice was still playing a reply.

conversation.no_first_token.description: The conversation layer produced no first token by filler_deadline_ms after EOT.

conversation.slow.description: Still no speakable chunk at holding_deadline_ms, or no first token at deferral_deadline_ms.

conversation.backgrounded.description: The host converted a slow turn into background work; the answer will arrive as an announcement.

conversation.react_hint.description: The conversation layer's first tokens carried a reaction hint (⟦react:laugh⟧ and similar), stripped before display.

stage.open.description: The owner opened Talk or this agent's desk stage by a click, Enter or tap.

stage.close.description: The owner left Talk or this agent's desk stage.

floor.hover.dwell.description: Pointer rested on a desk tile for hover_dwell_ms below the speed threshold, or a tap on a face on touch devices.

floor.focus.dwell.description: Keyboard focus rested on a desk tile or Directory row for keyboard_dwell_ms.

attention.contention.description: The owner addressed an agent whose voice or floor is busy on another thread (from attention.changed).

attention.resumed.description: The agent's contended voice or floor became free and it returns to the owner's thread.

job.progress.description: A job or step passed a checkpoint (new running sentence, step n of m).

job.steered.description: An owner steer was queued or applied at a checkpoint.

job.done.description: A job or step finished with a result.

step.retry.description: A tool call or step attempt failed and is being retried.

step.blocked.description: A step is blocked: missing key or connector, cap hit, failed after retries, Everyone stop.

handoff.description: handoff event: from → to with a note.

ask.description: ask event: asker → target with a task.

ask.answered.description: The target's answer to an ask.

verdict.description: A reviewer's JSON verdict on a coworker's work.

deliverable.accepted.description: The owner accepted a deliverable (as-is or with edits).

decision.resolved.description: The owner resolved a raised hand (approved or declined).

room.owner_floor.description: The owner raised a hand or took the floor in a voiced room; the moderator yields.

sidetalk.opener.description: A side-talk opener was shown; its counterpart may reply.

quiet.summary: Functional reflexes only. Acknowledgements, fillers, juggling notices and replies still speak; expressive reactions become face-only; no passing-by talk, no side-talk, no quips.

lively.summary: The default. Owner-directed reflexes are voiced; passing-by hellos show as bubbles and speak softly when voice is on; side-talk appears as bubbles and is voiced only while you listen in to that pod; quips are rare.

buzzing.summary: A busy office. Side-talk is voiced on the Floor for an owner who touched it in the last two minutes (after ten minutes of passive watching it falls back to Lively), banter replies can chain to three lines, passing-by cooldowns are shorter and quips more frequent.

owner_name.source: The member's first name from Settings. Never a guest's name.
owner_name.description: Pre-voiced per agent once the owner has a name; stored under the workspace prefix, never the shared one.

chief_name.source: WorkspaceSettings.chiefName, else the lead's catalog first name.
chief_name.description: Used by coworkers ('Morgan asked me to…').

coworker.source: First name of the counterpart agent in the triggering event (handoff, ask, verdict, result).

project.source: Project short name (≤ 3 words) from the project row; Everyday is never spoken.

client.source: The project's client tag display name.

step_label.source: The running sentence of the agent's current step or job (route-table running copy or job.progress label), verb-first, first letter lowercased, trailing period removed.
step_label.description: Grounds passing-by and micro-status in real work.

artifact.source: Deliverable or job output name from the cause event.

done.source: job.progress step (integer), spoken as a word up to twelve.
done.description: Numbers above twelve are rendered at runtime.

total.source: job.progress of (integer); the slot is unresolvable when the total is unknown.

eta.source: Bucketed from a real remaining-time estimate (remaining audio, floor turn, job forecast); unresolvable without one.
eta.description: Buckets: <4 s, 4-12 s, 12-20 s, 20-45 s, 45-90 s, 90-240 s. Longer waits never use a reflex.

other_thread.source: Short noun phrase for the agent's other attention thread, from its label ('the Northwind review', 'a question from Pax').

blocker.source: The blocked reason in ≤ 6 words from the step.blocked event ('HubSpot needs a sign-in').
blocker.description: Never invented or paraphrased beyond the event's own copy.

finding_count.source: Number of findings in the verdict, spoken as a word.

part_of_day.description: Late night uses its own lines, never 'night' as a greeting.

gist.source: ≤ 60-character summary of the real event (handoff note, ask task, answer, result summary) passed through sanitizeGist.
gist.description: Side-talk only; bubble text always, voice only for an observer.

contexts.weekday:*: Owner-local weekday: monday … sunday. Use workweek:* for anything that assumes a working week or a weekend off.
contexts.workweek:*: first_day | last_day of the workspace's working week (Settings work_days, default Monday-Friday): the first working day after a day off, the last one before a day off.
contexts.weekend: Today is not one of the workspace's working days.
contexts.works_weekends: The workspace's working days include Saturday or Sunday.
contexts.first_meeting: The owner has never exchanged a turn with this agent.
contexts.returning: The owner's last activity in the workspace was 3 h or more ago.
contexts.new_day: First stage open of the owner-local day.
contexts.working: The agent is running a step or job (presence working or thinking).
contexts.idle: The agent has no open work.
contexts.unstaffed: The agent is in the Directory but on no team yet.
contexts.in_meeting: The agent is a participant in a live meeting.
contexts.after_win: This agent or its team had a win (accepted deliverable, approve verdict, project done, approved raised hand) in the last 30 min.
contexts.after_blocker: The agent was unblocked in the last 30 min.
contexts.unblocked_by:*: owner | coworker | system: who caused the last step.unblocked (the owner, or a decision the owner approved; a coworker's answer; a retry or a connector recovering). Only unblocked_by:owner lines may thank the owner.
contexts.has_updates: There are ledger events the owner has not seen since their last visit; greetings that promise a report require it.
contexts.streak: Three or more wins for this agent today.
contexts.high_load: The agent holds three or more attention threads.
contexts.steer_queued: The owner's steer is queued for the next checkpoint.
contexts.interrupted: The agent's previous line was cut by the owner.
contexts.owner_farewell: The owner's turn is a farewell.
contexts.owner_greeting: The owner's turn is a greeting.
contexts.own_error: The conversation layer marked the previous answer as this agent's own error.
contexts.owner_question: The owner's turn is a real question (a '?' or a question word, and not a request phrased as one). Lines that praise a question require it.
contexts.owner_praise: The owner praised the agent's work (praise cue ≥ 0.6). Thank-you-back and modest replies require it.
contexts.owner_gratitude: The owner thanked the agent (gratitude cue ≥ 0.6).
contexts.owner_self_doubt: The owner doubted themselves out loud ('am I crazy', 'is this a dumb question').
contexts.owner_tone:*: positive | neutral | negative: the sniffer's read of the owner's turn. negative = bad news, frustration, a correction or distress ≥ 0.3. Evaluative acknowledgements forbid owner_tone:negative.
contexts.topic:*: The owner's turn mentions one of this agent's own topics (signature pack `topics`, e.g. topic:hospitality). Domain-flavoured reactions require it.
contexts.eta_known: A real remaining-time estimate exists (the eta slot resolves).
contexts.step_ing: The step label reads as a gerund phrase ('reading 14 reports'), so it can follow 'Still', 'Busy', 'Just' or 'I'm'.
contexts.reply_to:*: Side-talk reply to an opener: handoff_give, ask_coworker, answer_coworker, share_result, review_approve, review_changes, celebrate; reply_to:any fits every opener. A sidetalk_reply line must carry one.
contexts.activity:*: Activity type of the current step (catalog activity_types: research, analysis, document, llm, review, image, video, app, meeting, files, …).
contexts.role:*: The agent's role on the current team (lead, co_owner, reviewer, sceptic, facilitator, specialist) or role:chief for the Chief of Staff.
contexts.quiet_hours: The workspace is inside its quiet hours.

sincere_ai: am i talking to a person

intents.summary: A tiny listener sound while the owner speaks ('mm-hm', 'right'), played only inside a real pause, softly, never as agreement to a decision.

triggers.when: Pause of 350-1000 ms inside an utterance to this agent, after at least 2.5 s of owner speech, with no agent audio playing.

honesty: Never words that consent or approve ('yes, do it', 'agreed'): a backchannel signals listening, not agreement.
Cancelled the instant the owner resumes; it never talks over the owner.

intents.summary: A short receipt of a request, steer or correction ('On it.', 'Noted — I'll fold that in at the next step.') before the real reply streams.

triggers.when: Voice turn whose request cue is ≥ 0.6 and no stronger reaction won.
The owner's steer was queued for the next checkpoint.
The new message is a stop or steer: the agent yields at the sentence boundary and acknowledges.

honesty: Acknowledges receipt only; never says the thing is done ('Done.' is forbidden here).
steer_queued lines must say the change lands at the next step, never that it already has.
Plays before any model has read the turn: an evaluative ack ('love this one', 'ooh, fun') forbids owner_tone:negative (E4).
examples: Noted — I'll fold that in at the next step.
Mm, okay. Give me a moment on that.

intents.summary: Covers conversation-layer latency: plays when no first token has arrived 700 ms after the owner's turn ('Mm, give me a sec.'). Capped by the agent's p50 first-chunk latency, so fast brains get short fillers.

triggers.when: Voice exchange; no first token 700 ms after EOT (1800 ms if an acknowledgement or reaction already played); not after 2200 ms.
Text exchange; still no first token 2500 ms after Send: a caption bubble under the face, not voiced.

honesty: Never promises an answer's content ('great news coming') or claims to be checking something the brain is not using.
Plays before any model has read the turn: a line that praises a question ('good question') requires owner_question (E4).
examples: Hmm. [pause] Let me think about that properly.

intents.summary: A second, calmer hold when the reply is still not speakable 3.5 s after the turn ('Still with you — nearly there.').

triggers.when: No speakable chunk at 3500 ms after EOT and at least 800 ms since the previous reflex ended.

honesty: No false progress ('almost done') unless the stream has actually started.
examples: Bear with me — this one has a few moving parts.

intents.summary: An honest hand-back when a turn is too slow for live conversation and the host has moved it to background work ('This needs a proper look — I'll come back to you in a couple of minutes.').

triggers.when: No first token by 8000 ms and the host converted the turn to background; the answer will arrive as an announcement.

honesty: Only when the host has really moved the work to the background; the promise must be kept by an announcement.
eta only from a real forecast; otherwise lines without a time.
examples: This one needs a proper look — I'll come back to you in {eta}.
Let me work on that properly and message you when it's ready.
I'll dig into that in the background and ping you.

intents.summary: A laugh or chuckle in the persona's own laugh style when the owner is being funny.

triggers.when: Humor cue ≥ 0.6 and no distress or frustration cue.
The conversation layer hinted laugh.

honesty: Laughter is with the owner, never at the owner: suppressed after distress, frustration, errors, or the owner's self-criticism.
Never laughs at a customer, a coworker or a third party.
examples: [laugh] Okay, I walked into that one.

intents.summary: A quick 'oh!' at news, as a lead-in to the real reply.

triggers.when: Good- or bad-news cue ≥ 0.6 with an exclamation, or an unexpected figure; no distress cue.
The conversation layer hinted surprise.

honesty: Surprise at the owner's news only, never feigned surprise at the agent's own results.

intents.summary: Warm pleasure at the owner's good news ('Oh, that's brilliant.').

triggers.when: Good-news or praise cue ≥ 0.6.
The conversation layer hinted delight.

honesty: Delight at the owner's news or praise; never claims the team caused the win unless a cause event says so.

intents.summary: A sober beat at the owner's bad news about the business ('Oof. Okay.'), before the real reply.

triggers.when: Bad-news cue ≥ 0.6 without distress (distress goes to sympathy).
The conversation layer hinted concern.

honesty: No catastrophising and no blame; the reply that follows carries the substance.
examples: Ah. Okay — let's look at it.

intents.summary: A soft, human acknowledgement of how the owner feels ('Long one, huh.'), and the only reaction allowed after distress.

triggers.when: Frustration ≥ 0.5 or any distress cue.
The conversation layer hinted sympathy.

honesty: Never claims to feel the owner's pain or to have lived the same thing ('I know exactly how you feel').
After distress: no jokes, no laughs, no quips for the rest of the session.
examples: That's a lot. Let's make it lighter.

intents.summary: A brief vote of confidence when the owner doubts themselves or a plan ('You've got this — and so do we.').

triggers.when: Doubt cue ≥ 0.6 without distress.
The conversation layer hinted encouragement.

honesty: Encourages without promising outcomes ('this will definitely work' is forbidden).
Never presupposes what the owner said: doubt fires on 'worried' or 'not sure', so no 'you're not crazy' (and never 'crazy' or 'dumb', E12). Lines about a question require owner_question.
examples: Hey — it's a good instinct. Let's test it.
It's a fair thought. Let's look at it together.

intents.summary: The reply to a purely phatic 'thanks' ('Anytime.'). It is the whole turn: the brain is not called, and the host records it as a message.

triggers.when: Gratitude or praise cue ≥ 0.8, phatic (≤ 6 words, no question, no request, no entity); decided by the host.

honesty: Only for phatic turns; 'thanks, and also…' goes to the brain.
Thanking back or modesty ('Aw, thanks!', 'Stop, you're too kind') requires owner_praise; a plain 'thanks' gets 'anytime' (E4).

intents.summary: A light social repair when the owner corrects the agent ('Ah — sorry, let me fix that.'), before the corrected reply.

triggers.when: Correction cue ≥ 0.7 right after this agent's reply.
The conversation layer hinted apology (context own_error when it judged the mistake its own).

honesty: Lines that admit fault ('My mistake.') need context own_error; otherwise use neutral repair ('Ah — got it.').
Never grovelling, never blaming the owner or another coworker.

intents.summary: Stopping for the owner. On voice barge-in it is face-only (the owner is talking); in a voiced room the moderator may yield aloud ('Go ahead, Dana.').

triggers.when: Owner speech confirmed over this agent's audio: face only, no voice.
The owner raised a hand or took the floor in a voiced room; only the moderator speaks the line.

honesty: Never voiced over the owner's own speech.

intents.summary: The human multitasking notice when the owner addresses an agent whose voice or floor is busy on another thread ('Hang on — finishing a thought in the review, back in ten seconds.').

triggers.when: The agent's voice or floor is busy on another thread with ≥ 2.5 s left; played at the next sentence boundary (≤ 4 s).
A new, non-steering question arrives while the current reply has 2.5-8 s left; the reply finishes, then the new one is answered.

honesty: Only with a real contention (one voice, one floor); never staged busyness.
eta and other_thread come from the attention view; lines without them are used when they do not resolve.
examples: Hang on — finishing a thought in {other_thread}, back in {eta}.
One sec, let me land this — then yours.

intents.summary: Returning to the owner after a juggle ('Okay — I'm all yours.').

triggers.when: The contended thread released and at least 6 s passed since the juggling line.

honesty: Never pretends to recall a topic it cannot name; no topic slot exists on purpose.

intents.summary: Hello when the owner walks up: first stage open of the day, after being away, or the very first meeting. Time-of-day aware.

triggers.when: First open of this agent's stage (Talk or desk) since 3 h idle or on a new owner-local day, with no owner input for 400 ms.
The owner has never exchanged a turn with this agent.
The owner's turn is only a greeting; the host answers with this line instead of calling the brain.

honesty: No claims about the agent's own night, weekend or commute.

Evening greetings never nag about brevity or rest (short, brief, quick, tight, rest, late): those belong to late_night (E15). Greetings that promise news require has_updates (E24); weekday lines that assume a weekend off use workweek:* (E14).
Never on page load: only after the owner's own click, Enter or tap opened the stage.
examples: Hi {owner_name}, I'm {self_name}. Good to meet you properly.

intents.summary: When the owner lingers on a desk on the Floor, the coworker looks up and says one short line grounded in what it is actually doing; the owner can answer inline.

triggers.when: Pointer rests ≥ 600 ms on the desk tile (tap on touch), the agent is not speaking and no foreground audio plays.
Keyboard focus rests ≥ 900 ms on the desk tile or Directory row; bubble only, never voiced.

honesty: Grounded in presence: working lines need a step_label or the working context, idle lines need idle, unstaffed lines need unstaffed.
Nothing added to the real step: no second activity after {step_label} ('Reading reviews', 'Tab, tab, tab'). Idle lines that ask for work set solicits: true (one per 10 min, Floor-wide, E25).
Blocked agents use the blocked intent instead.
examples: Quiet desk so far. Anything for me?
Hi — {self_name}. Nothing on my desk yet.

intents.summary: A tiny, true status update ('Three of five done.') when the owner looks in on a working agent or progress lands while the owner is at its stage.

triggers.when: Working desk whose job progress changed since the owner last saw it; replaces passing_by.
Progress lands while the owner is at this agent's stage.
A queued steer was applied at a checkpoint.

honesty: Numbers only from job.progress; a line with {total} is unusable when the total is unknown.
Never 'done' or 'sent': completion belongs to share_result and celebrate with a cause.

intents.summary: A light, personality-true remark about the kind of work they are doing, on the owner's approach in a good mood. Rare by design.

triggers.when: Working desk, mood valence ≥ 0.2, activity type known, not blocked and no blocker in the last 10 min; replaces passing_by with the ambience probability.

honesty: About the kind of work (activity context), never claims a specific result or finding.
Never about the owner, a customer or a coworker; never after distress in the session.
examples: Fourteen tabs open. All of them relevant, I promise.
Drafts are like pancakes — the first one's for the cook.

intents.summary: A short goodbye as the owner leaves after a real conversation, or answers a farewell.

triggers.when: The owner leaves after ≥ 2 turns in the last 10 min; plays as the stage closes.
Farewell cue; the host answers with this line if the turn is only a farewell.

honesty: Never 'I'll keep working all night' unless work is actually scheduled; never claims to go home or rest.

intents.summary: Side-talk opener when a coworker hands work to another: a pack opener plus the real hand-off gist ('Pax, it's yours — sources are in the folder.').

triggers.when: A handoff event the viewer can see, from → to, on a visible pod.

honesty: Only from a real handoff; the gist is the event's own note, sanitised.
Never mentions the owner.

intents.summary: The receiver's reply to a hand-off ('Got it, thanks.').

triggers.when: Reply to a handoff_give opener by its receiver.

honesty: Never claims to have started before the receiving step actually starts.

intents.summary: Side-talk opener for a real ask between coworkers: a pack opener plus the ask's gist ('Lena, quick one —').

triggers.when: An ask event the viewer can see, asker → target, on a visible pod.

honesty: The question shown is the real ask, trimmed; nothing is added.

intents.summary: The target's reply to an ask, opener plus the real answer's gist ('Sure — the March cohort.').

triggers.when: The target answered an ask shown as side-talk (or visible on the pod).

honesty: Timed to the real answer event, never ahead of it.

intents.summary: An author tells the next person in the plan that their piece is ready ('Grid's done — fourteen competitors, three surprises.').

triggers.when: A step finished with an artifact and the next consumer (next step owner or reviewer) is another coworker.

honesty: Only with an artifact on the cause event; the gist is the job's own summary.
Never 'sent', 'published' or 'shipped' to the outside world without a receipt.
examples: Over to you, {coworker}. It's in the folder.

intents.summary: A reviewer tells the author the work passed ('Looks solid. Nice work.').

triggers.when: Verdict approve on another coworker's work.

honesty: Only on a real approve verdict.
examples: Clean. Ship it to the next step.

intents.summary: A reviewer flags changes kindly ('Two notes on the pricing slide, {coworker}.'); the author replies with sidetalk_reply.

triggers.when: Verdict changes or block on another coworker's work.

honesty: Kind and specific-sounding without inventing specifics: counts only from the verdict.
Never mocking; scepticism is a badge, not a sneer.
examples: Close — a couple of fixes first.

intents.summary: A short reply to any side-talk opener: thanks, a laugh, an 'on it'. Context reply_to:<opener> picks the fitting lines.

triggers.when: The counterpart replies to an opener (chain limit per ambience).

honesty: Only replies to a real opener; never starts a thread on its own.
Every line carries reply_to:<opener> or reply_to:any. After review_changes or a block verdict the engine drops laughs, 'heh' and one-word shrugs (E7).

intents.summary: A real win lands: accepted deliverable, approved raised hand, project done, an approve verdict on own work. Owner-directed when the owner just acted at this agent's stage.

triggers.when: The owner accepted this agent's deliverable (exempt from budget when the owner is at its stage).
The owner approved this agent's raised hand.
The project finished; up to two teammates may join with sidetalk_reply (context reply_to:celebrate).

honesty: Celebrates what the cause event says happened, nothing more.
Sceptic-role agents celebrate quietly (intent weight 0.7).
examples: That's a good one to close out.
Nice. {artifact} is out of my hands and into yours.

intents.summary: An honest 'hm, stuck' when the agent's step is blocked, naming the real reason; the raised hand or Inbox card carries the actual request.

triggers.when: Shown when the owner is at the stage, or on the owner's next hover (replaces passing_by).

honesty: The reason is the event's own copy; no guessing.
Never escalates or pings: the interruption ladder does that.

intents.summary: Relief when a block clears ('Phew — back in business.').

triggers.when: A blocked step resumed; shown at the stage or on the next hover within 10 min.

honesty: Only after a real unblock event.
Thanks the owner only with context unblocked_by:owner: most unblocks are retries, a coworker's answer or a connector recovering (E18).

intents.summary: A small self-correction when an attempt fails and is retried while the owner is watching ('Hm, that didn't take — trying again.').

triggers.when: A retry while the owner is at this agent's stage or hovered its desk in the last 30 s.

honesty: Generic on purpose: no invented specifics about what went wrong.
examples: Hm, that didn't take — trying again.
Let me try that another way.
